name: CC430F5137IRGZR
title: MSP430 16-bit MCU with CC1101 sub-1 GHz radio core (CC430F613x, CC430F612x, CC430F513x)
summary: A family of single-chip wireless microcontrollers: an MSP430 CPUXV2 16-bit RISC core running up to 20 MHz, with up to 32 KB of flash and 4 KB of RAM, sharing the die with a radio transceiver built on the CC1101 (300 to 348 MHz, 389 to 464 MHz and 779 to 928 MHz, 0.6 to 500 kBaud, up to +12 dBm). Around the core sit two Timer_A blocks, an RTC, USCI_A0 and USCI_B0 serial ports, a 128-bit AES engine, a 32-bit multiplier, three DMA channels, Comparator_B and, on the F613x and F513x, a 12-bit ADC; the F61xx parts add a 96-segment LCD driver. The F61xx come in a 64-pin 9 mm VQFN (RGC), the F513x in a 48-pin 7 mm VQFN (RGZ).
key_figures: 1.8 V to 3.6 V (radio: 2.0 V to 3.6 V)

operation.text: Eight devices share the die: CC430F6137, F6135, F6127, F6126, F6125 in the 64-pin RGC VQFN, and CC430F5137, F5135, F5133 in the 48-pin RGZ VQFN. Flash is 32, 16 or 8 KB and RAM 4 or 2 KB. The F61xx have the LCD_B driver and 44 I/O; the F513x have no LCD and 30 I/O. The 12-bit ADC is on the F613x (8 external inputs) and F513x (6 external inputs); the F612x have none. Every device has TA0 (5 CCR), TA1 (3 CCR), USCI_A0, USCI_B0, Comparator_B, RTC_A, AES128, MPY32, CRC16, three DMA channels and the radio. Typical values are at VCC = 3.3 V and 25 °C unless stated.

The radio is the CC1101 design. Receive is low-IF: an LNA, quadrature down-conversion to IF, then conversion to digital, with gain control, fine channel filtering, demodulation and packet sync done digitally. Transmit synthesizes the RF directly. The synthesizer's LC VCO is entirely on the die, and a 90° shifter derives the I and Q local-oscillator signals. The 26 MHz crystal oscillator gives the synthesizer reference and clocks the ADC and the digital part. The CPU reaches data, configuration and status through memory-mapped registers; the baseband handles channel setup, packets and buffering in TX and RX FIFOs. It supports 2-FSK, 2-GFSK, MSK, OOK and shaped ASK, sync-word detection, address check, variable packet length, automatic CRC, clear-channel assessment before transmit, a digital RSSI, and synchronous or asynchronous serial modes for legacy protocols.

The radio needs VCC from 2.0 V to 3.6 V and PMMCOREVx at 2 or 3. Bands: 300 to 348 MHz, 389 to 464 MHz (392 MHz with a 27 MHz crystal) and 779 to 928 MHz. The crystal is 26 to 27 MHz, 10 to 20 pF load, under 100 Ω ESR, with a total tolerance of ±40 ppm typical. MDMCFG2.DEM_DCFILT_OFF = 1 trades about 2 mA of RX current for a few dB of sensitivity below 250 kBaud. Output power is set by PATABLE; the optimum codes per band are tabled.

RF_P and RF_N form a differential port, LNA input in receive and PA output in transmit. Seen towards the antenna the optimum differential load is 122 + j31 Ω at 315 MHz, 116 + j41 Ω at 433 MHz and 86.5 + j43 Ω at 868 and 915 MHz. The input RF level must stay at or under 10 dBm, and RF_P, RF_N, RBIAS and VCORE take no more than 2.0 V.

The MSP430 CPUXV2 is a 16-bit RISC core with sixteen registers: R0 is the program counter, R1 the stack pointer, R2 the status register, R3 the constant generator, R4 to R15 general purpose. Register-to-register instructions take one clock. There are seven source and four destination addressing modes, the original 51 instructions in three formats plus extended-address instructions; every instruction works on bytes or words. Peripherals sit on the data, address and control buses and are driven by any instruction.

One active mode and five low-power modes, chosen by software; any interrupt wakes the device, runs the handler and can return it to the low-power mode. AM: all clocks run. LPM0: CPU and MCLK off; ACLK, SMCLK and the FLL run. LPM1: as LPM0 with the FLL off. LPM2: CPU, MCLK, FLL and DCOCLK off, the DCO's DC generator still on, ACLK running. LPM3: as LPM2 with the DC generator off too. LPM4: everything including ACLK and the crystal oscillator stopped, all data kept. Fast wake-up from LPM2 to LPM4 (5 µs at fMCLK ≥ 4 MHz) needs the low-side supervisor and monitor in full-performance mode or off; in normal mode it takes 150 µs.

Vectors and the reset address occupy 0FFFFh down to 0FF80h. Reset (0FFFEh) has the highest priority, then the system NMI and user NMI, then the maskable sources from Comparator_B (60) down to AES (45). An instruction fetch from peripheral space causes a reset.

Main flash is bank 0, ending at 00FFFFh. Information memory is four 128-byte flash segments, Info A to Info D, at 001800h to 0019FFh; the device descriptor is at 001A00h to 001AFFh; the bootloader takes four 512-byte segments at 001000h to 0017FFh. RAM sector 0 is 001C00h to 0023FFh; 4 KB parts add sector 1 at 002400h to 002BFFh. Peripherals occupy 0000h to 0FFFh. Unlisted addresses are vacant and trigger the vacant memory interrupt.

The bootloader programs flash or RAM over a serial link, protected by a user password. It is entered by a set sequence on RST/NMI/SBWTDIO and TEST/SBWTCK; the UART BSL transmits on P1.6 and receives on P1.5.

Four-wire JTAG uses PJ.3/TCK, PJ.2/TMS, PJ.1/TDI/TCLK and PJ.0/TDO, shared with general I/O and enabled by TEST/SBWTCK; RST/NMI/SBWTDIO is also needed by the tools. Two-wire Spy-Bi-Wire uses TEST/SBWTCK as clock and RST/NMI/SBWTDIO as data. No external programming voltage is needed. TEST has a 60 kΩ typical internal pulldown. In JTAG mode pullups switch on automatically on TMS, TCK and TDI/TCLK.

Flash is programmed through JTAG, Spy-Bi-Wire, the bootloader or by the CPU itself, by byte, word or long word. Main memory is in 512-byte segments; information memory is four 128-byte segments. Segments can be erased one by one or all together, information memory singly or with main memory, and segment A can be locked on its own. Program and erase work from 1.8 V. The cumulative program time per 128-byte block is 16 ms at most; endurance 10⁴ cycles minimum, retention 100 years at 25 °C.
RAM is built from 2 KB sectors; each can be powered down completely (losing its data) and drops into low-power retention by itself when it can.

Sources: a 32768 Hz watch crystal (XT1 on P5.0/XIN and P5.1/XOUT, with integrated load capacitance of 2 to 12 pF or a bypass input), the VLO (about 9.4 kHz), the trimmed REFO (32768 Hz), the DCO stabilized by a digital FLL to a multiple of the crystal, and the radio's 26 MHz crystal oscillator (XT2) as high-frequency source. The DCO starts in under 5 µs. ACLK, MCLK and SMCLK can each take any source; ACLK is also available divided by 2 to 32 as a buffered output.

An on-chip regulator makes the core voltage VCORE at one of four levels set by PMMCOREVx (1.4, 1.6, 1.8 or 1.9 V typical in active mode); each level allows a higher MCLK: 8, 12, 16, 20 MHz, needing VCC of at least 1.8, 2.0, 2.2, 2.4 V. VCORE needs a 470 nF capacitor, with the DVCC capacitance at least ten times larger. Supervisors (SVS, which resets) and monitors (SVM, which only flags) watch both the supply and the core. A brownout circuit gives a clean reset at power-up and power-down. AVCC and DVCC should come from one source, within 0.3 V of each other.

Up to five 8-bit ports P1 to P5 plus PJ. Each bit is set independently as input, output or interrupt, with selectable pullup or pulldown and drive strength; P1 and P2 bits all have edge-selectable interrupts. Ports can be accessed by byte, or by word as pairs PA (P1, P2) and PB (P3, P4).

Any digital function of the timers, USCIs, clocks, comparator, DMA trigger and radio GDO outputs can be assigned to any pin of P1 to P3 through the PxMAPy registers; the defaults are tabled. PM_ANALOG disconnects a pin's digital input and output for analog use.

SYS handles power-on reset and power-up clear, NMI source selection, the reset and NMI vector generators (SYSRSTIV, SYSSNIV, SYSUNIV), bootloader entry and the device descriptors, and offers a JTAG mailbox for passing data to and from a debugger.

Three channels move data between addresses without the CPU, so the CPU can stay asleep while peripherals are serviced. Triggers include the timers, USCI receive and transmit flags, the ADC, the multiplier and the external DMAE0 pin.

WDT_A resets the system when its interval runs out, or can serve as an interval timer. CRC16 computes a CRC-CCITT signature. MPY32 multiplies 8-, 16-, 24- and 32-bit operands, signed or unsigned, with multiply-and-accumulate. The AES accelerator encrypts and decrypts 128-bit blocks with 128-bit keys to FIPS PUB 197 in hardware.
USCI_A0 does UART (with automatic baud-rate detection), IrDA and 3- or 4-pin SPI; USCI_B0 does I2C and 3- or 4-pin SPI. I2C runs to 400 kHz; UART bit clock to 1 MHz.

TA0 has five and TA1 three capture/compare registers, with PWM outputs, interval timing and interrupts on overflow and each register. Both can be clocked from ACLK, SMCLK, their TACLK pin or RFCLK/192, and the radio GDO1 and GDO2 signals feed TA0's CCI3B and CCI4B inputs. RTC_A is either a 32-bit counter with two cascadable 8-bit prescale timers, or a calendar clock that handles month lengths and leap years, with alarms and offset calibration.

REF supplies 1.5 V, 2.0 V or 2.5 V to ADC12_A, LCD_B and Comparator_B. Comparator_B supports slope conversion, battery supervision and monitoring of outside signals, with a 32-tap reference ladder and selectable power modes. ADC12_A (F613x, F513x) is a 12-bit SAR with sample select control and a 16-word conversion and control buffer that holds up to 16 results without CPU attention; channel 10 is the temperature sensor and channel 11 the AVCC/2 divider.

On the F61xx only: static, 2-, 3- and 4-mux drive of up to 96 segments, segment data held in its own memory, an integrated charge pump giving an LCD voltage independent of the supply with software contrast control, and per-segment blinking. LCDCAP/R33 must go to VSS if the LCD is unused; with the charge pump on it takes a 4.7 µF capacitor.

The embedded emulation module, S version, offers three memory-access breakpoints or triggers in hardware, one on CPU register writes, up to four triggers combined into complex ones, a cycle counter and per-module clock control.

A tag-length-value structure at 001A00h holds the device ID (51h 37h for CC430F5137, 51h 35h for F5135, 51h 33h for F5133, 61h 37h/35h for F6137/F6135, 61h 27h/26h/25h for F612x), die data, ADC calibration (gain, offset and temperature sensor readings at 30 °C and 85 °C per reference level; absent on the F612x) and reference calibration factors.

The exposed pad is the only ground connection and must be soldered to a solid ground plane. Keep the 32 kHz crystal close, with ground round XIN and XOUT and no other signals near or under them. The R_BIAS resistor must be 56 kΩ ±1%.
